newsitem.title: LEBANON: Palestinians should kill leadership - Hizbollah.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians should kill leadership - Hizbollah.

text.p: Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah on Friday urged Palestinians to kill their "treacherous and tyrannical" leadership for signing a peace deal with Israel.
Hizbollah (Party of God) chief Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah told a group rally in Beirut that the Palestinian people should "overthrow this (self-rule) authority and execute its leadership."

The rally marked "World Qods (Jerusalem) Day", the last Friday of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan dedicated to protests against the Jewish state by Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini in 1979.

Nasrallah addressed the rally in Beirut's Shi'ite Moslem southern suburbs -- a bastion of the group -- where hundreds of Hizbollah fighters marched on huge Israeli and U.S. flags laid out in the street.

He said a Palestinian Khaled Islmabouli was needed to make "traitors of Jerusalem pay a heavy price" -- a reference to the Egyptian Islamist who assassinated Egyptian President Anwar Sadat in October 1981 for signing peace with Israel in 1979.
A presenter introduced different guerrilla units including commandos in black uniforms and members of suicide squads with headbands and mock explosive packs.

"It has become obvious that the real problem is in the tyrannical leadership of the Palestinian people who will never break their chains of humiliation unless they punish and get rid of this treacherous leadership," Nasrallah said.
The Palestinian Authority -- headed by President Yasser Arafat -- signed an agreement for self-rule with Israel in Oslo in 1993.
Hizbollah guerrillas fight Israeli troops to oust them from a 15 km (nine miles)-wide south Lebanon occupation zone held by the Jewish state since 1978.
